message.content:
**Proteins that are typically found in the plasma membrane**

| Category | Protein (example) | Function / role |
|----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (sodium‑potassium pump) | Maintains the electrochemical gradients of Na⁺ and K⁺ across the membrane. |
| | • **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** | Facilitates passive diffusion of glucose into cells. |
| | • **Aquaporin‑4** | Water channel that allows rapid water movement. |
| | • **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β₂‑adrenergic receptor | Detect extracellular signals (hormones, neurotransmitters) and activate intracellular signaling cascades. |
| | • **Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs)** – e.g., epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) | Bind growth factors and trigger phosphorylation cascades that regulate cell proliferation. |
| | • **Integrins** – e.g., α₁β₁ integrin | Mediate cell–extracellular matrix adhesion and signal transduction. |
| | • **Cadherins** – e.g., E‑cadherin | Mediate calcium‑dependent cell–cell adhesion. |
| | • **Connexins** – e.g., connexin 43 | Assemble into gap junction channels that allow direct cytoplasmic communication between adjacent cells. |
| | • **Ion channels** – e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv1.1), voltage‑gated Ca²⁺ channel (Cav1.2) | Permit selective ion flow in response to voltage changes or ligand binding. |
| | • **Transporters** – e.g., cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) | Move ions or small molecules across the membrane (CFTR is a chloride channel). |
| | • **Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) class I & II** | Present peptide antigens to immune cells. |
| | • **Tetraspanins** – e.g., CD9, CD81 | Organize membrane microdomains and modulate signaling. |
| | • **Receptor tyrosine phosphatases** – e.g., PTPµ | Dephosphorylate tyrosine residues on target proteins. |
| | • **Scaffold proteins** – e.g., PSD‑95 (postsynaptic density protein 95) | Anchor receptors and signaling molecules at synapses. |
| **Peripheral (non‑integral) proteins** | • **Ankyrin** | Links integral membrane proteins to the spectrin-actin cytoskeleton. |
| | • **Spectrin** | Provides structural support and maintains membrane shape. |
| | • **Band 3 protein (anion exchanger 1)** | Transports Cl⁻/HCO₃⁻ across erythrocyte membranes; peripheral but tightly associated with the cytoskeleton. |
| | • **Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) adaptor proteins** – e.g., Grb2 | Bind to phosphorylated receptors and recruit downstream signaling molecules. |
| | • **Glycophorin A** (erythrocyte) | Peripheral protein involved in cell–cell interactions and membrane stability. |
| | • **Mucin‑like proteins** – e.g., MUC1 | Extend into the extracellular space and protect the cell surface. |

---

### How to use this list

- **Research**: If you’re studying a particular cell type, look for the proteins most relevant to its function (e.g., GLUT1 in neurons, CFTR in airway epithelial cells).
- **Drug targeting**: Many drugs target plasma‑membrane proteins (e.g., β‑blockers target β‑adrenergic GPCRs, kinase inhibitors target RTKs).
- **Diagnostics**: Surface markers (e.g., CD antigens) are used in flow cytometry to identify cell populations.

Feel free to ask for more details on any specific protein or category!
